The reduction ran clean and wrote `evidence/20260929_loop081_bound/run672/summary.json`. Every guard in the script passed, including the strict ones: 48/48 requests succeeded with exactly 1024 output tokens and no errors in all six benches, the 128 `rank*_cohort*.json` files per arm cover all `(rank 0-7) × (cohort 1-16)` exactly once, the 8 ranks agree on cycle count within each cohort, all 12 sequences generated 1024 tokens, `target_graph_mode` contains `FULL` with `host_mirror_exact`, input-token counts match pairwise between arms, all 9 cleanup/restore exit codes are 0, and the before/after sha256 manifests for both source and scripts are byte-identical.

**Headline result: bounded input-token memoization measures +4.2% median output TPS (587.3 → 612.0 over 48×32K→1024, c12), but essentially all of that comes from a host-side residual reduction, not from device cycles.**

The decomposition is the part worth attending to:

| | cacheoff (mean) | cacheon (mean) |
|---|---|---|
| rank0 ms/cycle | 56.72 | 57.44 |
| rank0 cycles per 48-req cohort | 1188.7 | 1208.3 |
| rank0 residual (client_s − cohort wall) | 16.66 s | 12.02 s |

Runtime per cycle is flat to slightly *worse* under cacheon, and cycles are 1.6% *higher*, so the token-per-cycle ratio did not improve. The entire gain sits in the ~16.7 s → ~12.0 s of rank0 wall time not accounted for by cohort execution — that residual is the host-side non-fixed-serving work the cache is meant to remove. The residual drop is consistent in all three repeat pairs (16.48/16.62/16.87 → 11.38/10.71/13.97), which is the strongest evidence in this run that the mechanism is real rather than noise.

The caveat I'd flag before treating +4.2% as the number: that statistic is fragile. The cacheon arm's own spread (617.8 / 612.0 / 582.4) is three times wider than cacheoff's (577.9 / 587.3 / 588.7), and cacheon's worst repeat (582.4) falls *below* cacheoff's median (587.3). On means instead of medians the effect is +3.3% (584.6 → 604.1). With n=3 per arm and overlapping ranges, this run does not by itself establish a confidence interval excluding zero — the robust finding here is the host-residual reduction, and the TPS delta should be read as consistent with, but not independently proving, a 3-4% Product gain.

limits: Separate launches and batching may change acceptance trajectory. Residual includes all non-fixed-serving Product work; useful tokens/cycle ratio includes prebulk outputs. No exact generated-text parity claim.
